newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures close up, eyes on US heating oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures close up, eyes on US heating oil.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended the day firmer as dealers watched the price of U.S. heating oil surge higher and higher, continuing a bull run dating from June.
November Brent closed at $23.19 a barrel, 24 cents up from Tuesday, after briefly touching a high of $23.32.
October gas oil closed $1.75 higher at $225.00 a tonne, after touching a high of $228.00 earlier in the day.
"It's heating oil in the (United States,) one IPE dealer said. "Everyone is going bananas trying to buy it and that is pulling everything else up with it."
Heating oil gained support from the latest weekly data from the American Petroleum Institute (API,) which showed a modest 303,000 barrel build in stocks, well below expectations.
Recent gas oil arbitrage trade to Europe has served as a brake on replenishment of heating oil stocks in the U.S., which the API said were almost 19 million barrels down on year-ago levels.

Gasoline futures recovered ground lost earlier in the day then moved higher, also in the wake of heating oil, despite a bearish weekly build of over three million barrels, and news of fresh arbitrage cargo trade from Europe.
"It is heating oil which has led to strength all round," one trader said.
